edits.text: 1. Purchase Price. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD 42,000,000 for the Shares.

3. Representations; Disclosure Schedules; Bring-Down; Remedy. Except as specifically disclosed in the disclosure schedules delivered by the Seller to the Buyer at signing, the Seller represents that the financial statements fairly present, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of their respective dates and its results of operations for the periods then ended. The Seller's representation in this Section 3 shall be true and correct in all material respects as of Closing as though made at Closing, except to the extent it expressly relates to an earlier date. Subject to the limitations in this Section 3, the Seller shall indemnify the Buyer for losses arising from a breach of this representation. The Buyer must give written notice describing any claim in reasonable detail within 12 months after Closing. The Seller shall have no liability unless aggregate covered losses exceed one percent of the Purchase Price, in which case the Seller shall be liable only for losses exceeding that amount; the Seller's aggregate liability under this Section 3 shall not exceed ten percent of the Purchase Price. The foregoing claim period, threshold, and cap shall not apply to the Seller's fraud.

receiver.requested_changes: Reduce the purchase price to USD 38,000,000. Require delivery and Buyer review of specific disclosure schedules before signing, with no general or implicit disclosures. Require the financial-statement representation to be accurate at Closing without an additional materiality qualification. Extend the claim-notice period to 24 months, reduce the loss threshold to 0.5% of the purchase price and make it a tipping basket, and raise the liability cap to 20% of the purchase price. Preserve the fraud exception.
